extra.message: SQL Injection in /select endpoint: User-supplied 'username' parameter is directly concatenated into SQL query using f-string. An attacker can inject SQL payloads like '" OR "1"="1" to bypass authentication or extract data.

SQL Injection in /user PUT endpoint: All user-supplied fields (name, username, password, address, email, contact) are directly interpolated into SQL INSERT query using f-strings without parameterization. Attackers can inject SQL code through any of these fields.

SQL Injection in /user DELETE endpoint (username path): User-supplied 'username' parameter is directly concatenated into SQL DELETE query using f-string. Allows arbitrary SQL execution and data deletion.

SQL Injection in /user DELETE endpoint (user address path): User-supplied 'user.address' is directly interpolated into SQL DELETE without quotes or parameterization. Also missing quotes around the value.

NoSQL Injection in /find GET endpoint: User-supplied 'username' parameter is passed directly to MongoDB-style find() query. Attackers can use NoSQL operators like {'username': {'$ne': null}} to bypass authentication.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: NoSQL Injection in /find POST endpoint: The entire JSON request body is passed directly to NoSQL find() without validation. Attackers can send arbitrary MongoDB operators like {'$where': '...'} to execute JavaScript or extract all data.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: Missing Authentication on critical /reset POST endpoint: Anyone can reset the entire database without authentication. Lines 244-245 delete database files (remove and rmtree operations). No auth checks present.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Broken Access Control / IDOR in /user DELETE endpoint: No authentication or authorization checks. Any user can delete any other user by username. Allows mass deletion of user accounts without verification.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Insecure Password Hashing: MD5 algorithm is used for password hashing at line 113. MD5 is cryptographically broken and vulnerable to rainbow table attacks. Should use bcrypt, Argon2, or PBKDF2.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
